title: Index Signatures Enabling Prototype Pollution
platform_conditions: Compiles to plain JavaScript property assignment; prototype-chain semantics of the runtime apply wherever the emitted JS runs
security_mechanism: Record<string, T> and index-signature types tell the checker any key is acceptable, so map[userKey] = value compiles without question even when userKey is '__proto__'; at runtime that assignment re-points the object's prototype exactly as in the JavaScript prototype-pollution class. Without noUncheckedIndexedAccess, reading users[attackerId] is typed as T rather than T | undefined, so the undefined a miss returns propagates into authorization code as if it were a real record -- and a falsy-but-typed value can pass the wrong check.

source_sink_clues.source: Client-supplied keys (field names, column names, path segments) used to index or write into typed dictionaries.
source_sink_clues.sink: obj[attackerKey] = value on plain objects typed with index signatures; unguarded reads typed T from Record<string, T> feeding security decisions

tracking_guards: Check keys are validated against an allowlist or matched against a key-pattern grammar before indexing; check storage uses Object.create(null) or Map<string, T>; check noUncheckedIndexedAccess is enabled so reads are T | undefined and handled.
not_candidate_when: The key comes from a fixed enum or allowlist, the container is a Map or null-prototype object immune to prototype writes, or the indexed value is re-validated after the read.
synthetic_vulnerable_example: const map: Record<string, any> = {}; map[userKey] = value;
synthetic_safe_example: const map = new Map<string, any>(); map.set(userKey, value);
public_references: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1321.html
TypeScript Handbook: More on Functions & Object Types (index signatures) — https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/objects.html
